rows.label: Concept
rows.text: A detailed examination of the eukaryotic cell shows how each membrane-bound organelle specialises a metabolic function. The fluid-mosaic plasma membrane controls transport; mitochondria and chloroplasts convert energy (and carry their own DNA, evidence of endosymbiosis); RER makes protein while SER makes lipid; the Golgi modifies and packages; lysosomes digest; the nucleus and nucleolus control heredity; and the…

rows.label: Formula
rows.text:
Fluid-mosaic: phospholipid bilayer + integral/peripheral protein + cholesterol + glycocalyx
Protein secretion: ribosome → RER → Golgi → vesicle → exocytosis
Mitochondrial respiration: glycolysis → Krebs → ETS → ~34 ATP

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: RER makes PROTEIN; SER makes LIPID. A cell secreting lots of protein has abundant RER + Golgi (e.g., pancreatic acinar cell).  ·  The Golgi does NOT synthesise proteins; it MODIFIES, SORTS, and PACKAGES what the RER made.

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: NEB written answers expect a labelled organelle diagram + a one-line function per organelle.  ·  The endosymbiotic theory (4 evidence lines: own DNA, 70S ribosomes, double membrane, binary fission) is a favourite 4-mark question.

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: Secretory protein pathway: ribosome (free) → RER → Golgi → transport vesicle → plasma membrane (exocytosis).  ·  Mitochondrial respiration: glucose → pyruvate (cytoplasm) → Krebs (matrix) → ETS (cristae) → ATP.

rows.label: Limitation
rows.text: Mitochondria and chloroplasts have their OWN DNA + 70S ribosomes — the key endosymbiosis evidence.  ·  Lysosomes are animal-cell organelles; plants use the large vacuole for hydrolytic digestion.

rows.label: Derivation
rows.text: Label a plant cell (all organelles)  ·  Differentiate RER/SER

rows.label: Shortcut
rows.text: RER = rough = protein; SER = smooth = lipid.  ·  Mito + Chloro = own DNA + 70S ribosomes = endosymbiosis.

rows.label: Key points
rows.text: Each organelle has a distinct, examinable function (mitochondrion→ATP, chloroplast→photosynthesis, RER→protein, SER→lipid, Golgi→packaging, lysosome→digestion, nucleus→inheritance).  ·  RER = rough = ribosomes = protein; SER = smooth = no ribosomes = lipid.  ·  Mitochondria + chloroplast: own DNA, 70S ribosomes, double membrane, binary fission (endosymbiosis).  ·  Protein-secretion pathway: ribosome → RER → Golgi → vesicle → membrane.

rows.label: Universal facts
rows.text: The liver cell contains over a million ribosomes.  ·  Mitochondria and chloroplasts reproduce by binary fission, like bacteria.

rows.label: More practice
rows.text: Describe the protein-secretion pathway in a cell.  ·  Explain the endosymbiotic theory with evidence.  ·  State the role of the nucleolus.

rows.label: More hints
rows.text: Explain the endosymbiotic theory with 4 evidence lines.  ·  Trace the protein-secretion pathway.

rows.label: Extra solved
rows.text: Chloroplast photosynthesis: light reactions in grana → ATP + NADPH; Calvin cycle in stroma → glucose.  ·  Lysosome autophagy: damaged mitochondrion → autophagosome → lysosomal digestion → recycled.

rows.label: Study notes
rows.text: DETAILED ORGANELLE ANALYSIS (plant + animal cell).  ·  Plasma membrane: phospholipid bilayer (heads out, tails in) + integral proteins (channels, pumps, receptors) + peripheral proteins + cholesterol + glycocalyx (cell recognition). Fluid-mosaic model (Singer & Nicolson, 1972).  ·  Mitochondrion: double membrane; outer smooth, inner folded into cristae; matrix with Krebs enzymes; own DNA + 70S ribosomes (endosymbiosis); aerobic respiration: glycolysis (cytoplasm) → Krebs (matrix) → ETS (cristae) → ~34 ATP.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: 9+9 axoneme (cilia/flagella); 9+0 centriole  ·  Plant cell: wall + chloroplast + large central vacuole; animal cell: centrioles + lysosomes + small vacuoles.  ·  Cytoskeleton: microfilaments, intermediate filaments, microtubules.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Nucleus: envelope + nucleolus + chromatin; chromatin condenses to chromosomes in division.  ·  Cilia and flagella share the 9+9 axonemal microtubule structure; centrioles (9+0) are related but lack the central pair.  ·  The nucleus is NOT the only place with DNA: mitochondria + chloroplasts carry their own genomes.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Trace the secreted-protein pathway step by step.  ·  Contrast plant vs animal cell (wall, chloroplast, large vacuole vs centrioles, lysosomes).  ·  RER/SER distinction is a very common short-answer.
